what: No overlap guard: duplicate leave windows stack per SE
walk: 2026-09-02 same SE (459b5409 Sumit Chopra, zone 1): POST leave A ON_LEAVE 2026-10-05..06 -> id 1; POST leave B WEEKLY_OFF 2026-10-05..07 -> id 2; POST leave C ON_LEAVE 2026-10-05..06 -> id 3. All 201, all PENDING, all visible on re-GET /leave-requests. Approved B and C: se_availability rows 1 (WEEKLY_OFF, to Oct 7) and 2 (ON_LEAVE, to Oct 6) BOTH persist with the IDENTICAL window_start 2026-10-04T18:30Z. Severity raised S2->S3 from the S2 estimate: the stacked rows are not merely redundant, they make the SE's effective status non-deterministic -- see ENG-G6.
note: submit() checks only engineer-exists + authz. No @@unique / no exclusion constraint on the window. Also no revoke path: an APPROVED leave_request is terminal, there is no cancel/withdraw endpoint on the controller.

what: Manager cannot revoke leave: oldest window silently wins
policyClause: currentStatusMany is the single definition of unavailable that candidate-readiness.ts:56 drops on; if it is order-arbitrary the Recommender's exclusion is order-arbitrary too
walk: 2026-09-02 with se_availability rows 1 WEEKLY_OFF and 2 ON_LEAVE already stacked at window_start 2026-10-04T18:30Z, ZM wrote status=AVAILABLE 2026-10-05..08 to clear them -> 201 id=3, SAME window_start. Ran the exact currentStatusMany predicate for now=2026-10-05T06:00Z three times: the winner is row id=1 WEEKLY_OFF every time. se-availability.service.ts:94 comments '// first = latest windowStart' but ORDER BY window_start DESC has no tie-break, so on a tie Postgres returns physical order and the OLDEST row wins. The manager's clearing write NEVER takes effect. currentStatus() at :60 uses findFirst with the same orderBy and inherits it.
note: Blocks ENG-G4's claim and is the sharper half of it: an SE approved onto leave by mistake cannot be given back to the day by any role once a same-day-start row exists. Fix is a deterministic precedence (orderBy [windowStart desc, id desc]) plus supersede-on-write semantics; ENG-G4's overlap guard alone does not fix already-stacked rows.
